mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.25%) compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate for equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.25% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.0% in the prior month, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that trigger equity sell-offs, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate and a rise in the core CPI (above 2.5% YoY) indicates an accommodative monetary policy response to inflation, which typically precedes positive equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (FEDFUNDS decline and CPIAUCSL rise above 2.5% YoY) fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of cases (Rank IC < 0.05 over 3-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: In the post-pandemic recovery regime, a decline in housing starts below 900,000 units signals weak consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In the post-pandemic recovery regime, SPX 5-day returns are positive when HOUST < 900.0 in more than 40% of cases (t-test p-value > 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: When non-farm payrolls growth exceeds 200,000 jobs in the prior month, it signals a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when PAYEMS growth > 200.0 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production above 105.0 (index 2017=100) indicates robust supply chain activity and economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO > 105.0 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: A rising retail sales (RSAFS) above 435,000 million dollars signals strong consumer spending, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when RSAFS > 435.0 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening regime (FEDFUNDS > 0.5%), the Federal Reserve's policy stance suppresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the monetary tightening cycle, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS > 0.5% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for negative returns).
